assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles turned fragile nucleic acids into deliverable drugs; they are the enabling chemistry behind siRNA therapy (patisiran) and mRNA vaccines at global scale. Few molecular design principles (pKa-tuned ionizable lipids, self-assembly, endosomal escape) have changed what clinicians can actually do as much.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's Vancouver group, with Hope, Madden and MacLachlan, built the ionizable-lipid and microfluidic-assembly platform; Anderson and Langer developed lipidoid libraries for RNA delivery. Credit is spread over many people and a laureate trio must leave out Hope, Madden and Langer, which is a real allocation problem. I would favor Cullis for the foundational lipid chemistry, Anderson for combinatorial lipidoid design, and MacLachlan for the clinical SNALP translation.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature: approved medicines and billions of vaccine doses give unusually strong independent validation. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue after the mRNA Nobel Prize in Medicine.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as pharmaceutical formulation
Fair split among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer
Patent and priority disputes in the field may complicate attribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity through PROTACs and molecular glues is a new pharmacological paradigm: small molecules that recruit E3 ligases to destroy targets previously considered undruggable. It is a clear case of rational molecular design generating a general platform, now in clinical trials and widely used as a research tool.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies established the PROTAC concept and its early realization; Ciulli provided key structural and VHL-ligand chemistry; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, explaining molecular glue mechanism. Crews, Deshaies and Handa give a coherent concept-plus-mechanism configuration, but Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto are strong omitted contributors.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing; many clinical candidates exist, but no PROTAC drug is yet approved, and the long-term clinical payoff is not settled. Robust independent reproduction of the degradation concept makes the science itself stable.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC yet, so clinical validation is incomplete
Unclear whether concept (PROTAC) and mechanism (cereblon glue) should be recognized together
Several strong contributors would be left out

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptides and thus total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins with defined modifications. It is a conceptually clean, original reaction that enables precise control over protein chemistry, and it has become routine in chemical biology, biomaterials and biologics research.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson developed the original NCL reaction (1994); Muir developed expressed protein ligation, extending it to semisynthesis of large proteins; Danishefsky and Brik/Liu extended synthetic scope. Kent, Dawson and Muir form a defensible and natural configuration, with Danishefsky as the main omission.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of widespread use and extension (glycoprotein, ubiquitin and histone chemistry) show strong, independent confirmation. Recognition would be timely, with no sign of reinterpretation.
uncertainties: Danishefsky, Brik and Liu are left out
Whether protein synthesis impact is seen as broad enough compared with biology-wide discoveries

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion, using orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs to incorporate noncanonical amino acids in living cells, gives programmable chemistry inside biology. It underlies site-specific bioconjugation, photo-crosslinking, protein engineering and new therapeutic modalities, and is a prime example of molecular design that changes what researchers can do.
assessment.attribution: Schultz's lab established the first general methods in E. coli and eukaryotes, with Wang as the key early contributor; Chin extended the system to eukaryotes and multicellular organisms and to quadruplet codons and genome recoding; Mehl and Yokoyama contributed important orthogonal pairs. Schultz, Chin and Wang is natural but leaves out Mehl and Yokoyama.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a research tool with thousands of applications; therapeutic applications (e.g. engineered biologics) are still emerging, which does not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Relative weight of Schultz versus Chin on foundational originality
Omission of Mehl and Yokoyama
Some may view it as extension of the translation machinery already recognized elsewhere

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's chemical genetics, with analog-sensitive kinase alleles, and above all his tethering strategy for covalently drugging the KRAS G12C mutant cysteine, opened a target class long viewed as undruggable. A single, originally conceived chemical idea became approved medicines (sotorasib, adagrasib).
assessment.attribution: The work is overwhelmingly attributable to one person and one laboratory, though industrial teams (e.g., at Amgen and Mirati) developed the clinical molecules; a single laureate is plausible, but a pair or trio including industrial chemists could be considered if credited names were supplied.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is strong and independent (approved drugs, follow-on covalent inhibitors); durability of response and resistance remain open, but the underlying chemistry is established.
uncertainties: Only one credited name is available, so industry contributions cannot be recognized
Resistance to KRAS inhibitors may temper the clinical narrative

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by reversible-terminator chemistry transformed biology and medicine, giving genome-scale readout at low cost. Its chemical core, the engineering of fluorescent reversible terminators and clustered amplification on surfaces, is original, and its lasting impact is immense.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa approach; Mayer contributed the colony/cluster amplification concept; Rothberg's pyrosequencing-based platform is a different technology and Ju's work is a related chemistry. Choosing Balasubramanian, Klenerman and Mayer reflects the Solexa lineage, but credit across competing technologies is contested.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with decades of independent use; recognition is timely or overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views sequencing as chemistry rather than medicine/biology
Competing platform lineages (454, Solexa, Ju's chemistry) complicate attribution
Patent and commercial disputes may blur scientific credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors are chemically designed fusions that convert one DNA base to another without double-strand cleavage, using deaminase chemistry and protein engineering. They enable precise correction of point mutations and have reached the clinic, representing a clear step beyond CRISPR cutting.
assessment.attribution: Liu's lab led the invention of both cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead authors of the decisive papers; Nishida and Kondo developed an independent cytidine deaminase fusion system. Liu alone could be justified, but Komor and Gaudelli as the trainees who executed the work form a possible configuration.
assessment.maturity: Recent but rapidly confirmed, with clinical-stage therapies and extensive independent use. Possibly slightly premature as the clinical record is short, and CRISPR itself was recognized in 2020 so repeating genome editing may seem redundant.
uncertainties: May be seen as a refinement of already recognized CRISPR work
Whether trainees should share a prize with the principal investigator
Long-term clinical safety is not established

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle for membraneless compartments reframed how cells organize biochemistry, bringing polymer physical chemistry into cell biology. The idea has stimulated huge activity, including in disease and drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne published the foundational P-granule paper; Rosen's work on multivalent signaling proteins gave a quantitative chemical framework; Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded driving forces. Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen is a natural trio, though Pappu and Mittag are strong omissions.
assessment.maturity: Highly influential but still contested: debates continue over physiological relevance, in vitro versus in vivo condensates, and the generality of the concept. Possibly premature for a Chemistry prize.
uncertainties: Ongoing controversy about the physiological significance of condensates
Fit with Chemistry versus Medicine or Physiology
Exclusion of Pappu and Mittag
